note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up regarding recent hospitalization for infection concerns, spasms, lightheadedness, constipation, and diaphoresis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021 and discharged on 07/02/2021. During admission, patient presented with increasing spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. In the emergency department, she was febrile with significantly elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. There were concerns for urinary tract infection; however, patient believes her hospitalization was more likely due to dysreflexia from her quadriplegia. She experienced labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. Patient reports she did not have regular bowel movements during hospitalization but had significant bowel movement after discharge and felt much better. She attributes her symptoms to constipation rather than infection. Urine cultures obtained during admission were not impressive. Patient states she went to the emergency department due to out-of-control blood pressure causing headache and vomiting. She feels she has returned to her normal self since discharge. Today she denies pain or discomfort.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current pain or discomfort. Previously reported spasms, lightheadedness, constipation, diaphoresis, headache, vomiting, and blood pressure fluctuations during hospitalization, all now resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. Suprapubic catheter in place.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax daily for constipation; doubles dose when she does not have bowel movements. Lactulose for severe constipation ("rescue type thing"). Vitamin C. Multivitamins.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports staying indoors more during hot weather. Acknowledges the heat and humidity in late June may have contributed to her condition.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Patient able to take deep breaths and breathe normally. No pain or discomfort reported on examination.

RESULTS
Previous white blood cell count was elevated at 23,000 during hospitalization. Doctor notes that patient's white count is sometimes mildly elevated but was normal last year. Previous x-rays were obtained during hospitalization but no CT scan was performed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute to chronic constipation: Patient believes hospitalization was more likely due to dysreflexia from quadriplegia with associated vital sign changes rather than true urinary tract infection. Current bowel regimen with miralax as primary treatment and lactulose for severe constipation appears adequate. Will obtain updated fasting labs in 2-3 weeks including complete blood count to ensure white blood cells trend downward and to recheck cholesterol panel as patient is due for this screening. This will help determine if leukocytosis resolves or if something else is occurring with bowels.

Quadriplegia: Stable. Continue current management.

COVID vaccine status: Patient is currently unvaccinated. Discussed concerns about vaccine safety and unknown side effects. Patient reports she is young and healthy enough to beat COVID even with limited respiratory function and takes vitamin C and multivitamins. Doctor strongly recommended vaccination given patient's high-risk status due to quadriplegia. Explained that vaccine is safe, that side effects from vaccines in general exist but are rare (including Guillain-Barré), and that 50% of country has been vaccinated. Discussed that alternative treatments and monoclonal antibodies are not convincingly more helpful. Patient states she is open-minded and will consider. Doctor advised patient to think about it and reach out with any further questions. Patient to follow up in 2-3 weeks for labs.
